entries.section: 7.10 This community and the fayḍa
entries.heading: Q. 2:253 (FIR 2:3–9; locus 2:7)
entries.niasse: He says the umma agrees «أن محمدا صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم أفضل الأنبياء والمرسلين» and gives grounds over pp. 3–9. The locus (2:7) is the comparison of the ḥabīb with the khalīl: «الخليل من الخلة لأن الخليل تسد خَلته ويسد خلّتك» ("the khalīl comes from khalla, need, because the friend fills your need and you fill his"). Ibrāhīm asked for forgiveness, a good name, protection from idols; Muḥammad received these unasked. Ibrāhīm went by himself; Muḥammad was taken by night: «ذاك ذهب بنفسه وهذا أسري به بقدرة اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى من غير تكلف ولا مشقة» ("that one went by himself, and this one was taken by night by God's power, without effort or hardship"). He then draws the community into the same gift: «فلما كان عطاء محمد صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم وهبيا كذلك أمته» ("since what was given to Muḥammad was a free gift, so it is with his community"). Mūsā came to the appointment «فكان المجيئ منه مؤنة» ("so the coming was toil on his part"), while God showed the community His signs (Q. 41:53) «بالمعونة لا بالمؤنة» ("by assistance, not by toil") (2:7). Earlier (2:4) he grounds the umma's rank in the Prophet: «لماكنا خير أمة بسبب محمد صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم تبين أن محمدا أفضل من الأنبياء الذين أرسلوا إلى الأمم قبلنا».
entries.jalalayn: Read out in full (2:3): «فضل اللّٰه بعض الأنبياء على بعض بتخصيصه بمنقبة ليست لغيره», Mūsā as the one spoken to, and Muḥammad raised in rank «بعموم الدعوة وختم النبوة وتفضيل أمته على سائر الأمم والمعجزات المتكاثرة والخصائص العديدة». Niasse's grounds expand each item of this list (universal mission, seal, the umma's superiority, many miracles).
entries.sawi: not quoted in FIR at this verse; Ḥāshiya not in hand.
entries.ruhAlBayan: RB vol 1, offset c. 1060100–1063500. Ḥaqqī uses Jalālayn's own phrase («بأن خصصنه بمنقبة ليست لغيره») and then says prophets are equal in prophethood and differ in degrees. He makes Ibrāhīm «قطب التوحيد» because he alone called to the divine Essence, and Muḥammad follows him «باعتبار الجمع دون التفصيل». For rafaʿa baʿḍahum he means Muḥammad, citing the ḥadīth «فضلت على الأنبياء بست». The Taʾwīlāt najmiyya layer ranks prophets by the strength of their light over «ظلمات الوجود»; the Prophet's darkness was wholly effaced, so God called him nūr. RB has no khalīl/ḥabīb or maʿūna/maʾūna argument at this verse.
entries.relation: Jalālayn: extends. Niasse takes Jalālayn's list of the Prophet's merits as his outline and argues each point. RB: departs at this verse, but Niasse borrows from RB elsewhere. The maʿūna/maʾūna sequence (Ibrāhīm's going, Mūsā's coming, the Prophet's night journey, the community's being shown) is Ḥaqqī's ishāra on Q. 4:28 (RB vol 2, offset c. 521100): «أخبر عن ذهاب إبراهيم عليه السلام إلى حضرته باجتهاده وهو المؤونة» and, of this community, Q. 41:53 «وهو أيضاً بالمعونة وهي جذبات العناية». RB also contrasts Ibrāhīm's "I am going" (maqām) with the Prophet's night journey (mawhiba) at Q. 2:196 (vol 1, offset c. 840200): «فلما كان الخليل من أهل المقامات قال». Niasse moves this material to 2:253 and adds the ḥabīb/khalīl frame. Ḥaqqī's own reading here, Ibrāhīm as "pole of tawḥīd", would weaken Niasse's ranking, and Niasse does not mention it.

rulings.label: departs at this verse, but Niasse borrows from RB elsewhere

entries.section: 7.10 This community and the fayḍa
entries.heading: Q. 4:28 (FIR 2:165–67; locus 2:166–67)
entries.niasse: God wants four things for us: to make the sharīʿa clear, to guide us on the path «وهو الصراط إلى اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى», to accept our repentance «فنرجع إلى اللّٰه», and to lighten: «وأراد أن يخفف عنا وهذه أكبر نعمة عليا جعل التخفيف على محمد صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم وعلى أمته فصار سيرهم بالمعونة كما كان سير من قبلنا بالمؤْنة» ("and He willed to lighten for us; this is the greatest blessing on us [read علينا]: He placed the lightening on Muḥammad and his community, so that their journey went by assistance, as the journey of those before us went by toil"). He runs through Ibrāhīm (Q. 37:99), Mūsā (Q. 7:143), Muḥammad (Q. 17:1) and "us" (Q. 41:53), and concludes: «فمنعوا الوصل والوصال وأعطي محمد صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم الوصل والوصال» ("they were denied arrival and union, and Muḥammad was given arrival and union"), with the ḥadīth of the handspan for "us" (2:166). On khuliqa l-insānu ḍaʿīfan he builds an anthropology of weakness: the angel lives only in worship, the beast only in appetite, and the human cannot stay in any state: «فلضعفه وصل إلى أعلى مقام» ("through his weakness he reached the highest station"). God says «أنا ملِك حي لا يموت، ابن آدم إذا أطعتني جعلتك ملكا حيا لا يموت» ("I am a King, living, who does not die; son of Adam, if you obey Me I will make you a king, living, who does not die"). The same weakness makes him the worst of creatures: «هذا الضعف مدح في حق من أحبه اللّٰه وذم في حق من أبغضه اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى» ("this weakness is praise for the one God loves and blame for the one God hates") (2:167). He names those who follow lusts as «فرقة من قريش كانوا ينتقدون حكم الشريعة» who argued from cousins to nieces.
entries.jalalayn: Read out (2:165–66): those who follow lusts = «اليهود والنصارى والمجوس والزناة»; yukhaffifa = «يسهل عليكم احكام الشرع»; ḍaʿīfan = «لا يصبر عن النساء والشهوات».
entries.sawi: not quoted in FIR at this verse; Ḥāshiya not in hand.
entries.ruhAlBayan: RB vol 2, offset c. 519300–523800. Exoteric: ḍaʿīfan = unable to resist his desires; al-Kalbī «لا يصبر عن النساء». The occasion: «وقيل المجوس حيث كانوا يحلون الأخوات من الأب وبنات الأخ وبنات الأخت», with the same cousin/niece argument Niasse reports. The ishāra: God favoured this community with four things (tabyīn, hidāya, tawba, takhfīf); the fourth is «أن يوصلهم إلى حضرته بالمعونة ويخفف عنهم المؤونة». Then the same four proof-texts (37:99, 7:143, 17:1, 41:53), and «أن النبي يَكَِةِ وأمته مخصوصون بالوصول والوصال». RB then distinguishes: «الفرق بين النبي والولي في ذلك أن النبي مستقل بنفسه في السير إلى الله والوصول», while the saint walks only by following the Prophet. On weakness: «وهو ممدوح بهذا الضعف», the human is «ساعة بصفة بهيمة يأكل ويشرب ويجامع» and at another hour like an angel, neither angel nor beast can change state, and the ḥadīth «أنا ملك حى لا أموت أبداً عبدي أطعنى أجعلك ملكاً حياً لا يموت أبداً», so that he becomes the best or the worst of creatures (OCR «كين البرية» [read خير البرية]).
entries.relation: Jalālayn: extends (Niasse turns "cannot keep from women and lusts" into a doctrine of the human as the being with no fixed state). RB: follows, closely and without naming it. The four things, the maʿūna/maʾūna contrast, the four proof-texts in the same order, al-wuṣūl wa-l-wiṣāl, the handspan ḥadīth, the angel/beast/human triad, the ḥadīth of the living King, and "best/worst of creatures" all stand in Ḥaqqī's ishāra in this order. Side by side: RB «يوصلهم إلى حضرته بالمعونة ويخفف عنهم المؤونة» / Niasse «فصار سيرهم بالمعونة كما كان سير من قبلنا بالمؤْنة»; RB «وهو ممدوح بهذا الضعف» / Niasse «هذا الضعف مدح في حق من أحبه اللّٰه». Niasse departs on two points. He names a faction of Quraysh where Ḥaqqī and Jalālayn name the Magians. He drops Ḥaqqī's caution that the saint arrives only by following the Prophet, and he speaks of "us" as receiving the same assistance. He adds the rhetorical turn that weakness itself is the ground of the highest station.

rulings.label: follows, closely and without naming it

entries.section: 7.10 This community and the fayḍa
entries.heading: Q. 5:19 (FIR 3:46–47; locus 3:47)
entries.niasse: After Jalālayn's gloss he sets out a sacred chronology: «بين آدم ونوح ألف سنة، وبين نوح وإبراهيم ألف سنة» ("between Ādam and Nūḥ a thousand years, between Nūḥ and Ibrāhīm a thousand years"), Ibrāhīm to Mūsā two thousand, Mūsā to ʿĪsā a thousand, ʿĪsā to Muḥammad 569 or 600. He dates the present: «والآن بعد هجرة الرسول صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم ألف وثلاثمائة وثلاث وثمانون سنة» ("and now, after the Messenger's hijra, it is one thousand three hundred and eighty-three years"). Then: «والدنيا سبعة أيام وإن يوما عند ربك كألف سنة مما تعدون» and «سبعة آلاف سنة مضت لا تبلغ ألفا أبدا ولا علم إلا عند اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى» ("seven thousand years have passed; it will never reach a thousand; and there is no knowledge except with God") (3:47). The sentence is elliptical; it seems to say that the remaining span will not reach another thousand, but the printed text does not say this.
entries.jalalayn: Read out (3:46–47): «إذ لم يكن بينه وبين عيسى رسول ومدة ذلك خمسمائة وتسع وستون سنة», then «لو لم يأت محمد لقلتم ما جاءنا من بشير ولا نذير» (Niasse's paraphrase of Jalālayn's "lest you should say").
entries.sawi: The editor, at Niasse's chronology, says the dates are differing reports found in the tafsīrs «دون ترجيح لبعضها على بعض في الغالب» and refers to Ibn Kathīr, al-Qurṭubī and «حاشية الصاوي على الجلالين» 1:275–76 (3:47 n. 2). No wording from al-Ṣāwī is given.
entries.ruhAlBayan: RB vol 2, offset c. 1002100–1004300. Fatra = a lull in sending and a break in revelation; the verse is a favour, since they were sent a Messenger when the traces of revelation had worn away. God could send prophets in succession «كما فعل بين موسى وعيسى عليهما السلام حيث كان بينهما ألف وسبعمائة سنة وألف نبي», or after a gap as between ʿĪsā and Muḥammad (the figure is lost in the OCR). Then the story of Khālid b. Sinān from the Fuṣūṣ and the Prophet's birth.
entries.relation: Jalālayn: follows (569 years). RB: departs. Niasse's Mūsā–ʿĪsā interval (a thousand years) differs from RB's 1,700, and RB has no world-week or present-day dating. Niasse adds the dating to his own year (1383 AH, which the editor's n. 3 identifies as the year of the tafsīr) and sets the community near the end of a seven-thousand-year world. The same reckoning returns at Q. 10:3 and Q. 32:5.

entries.section: 7.10 This community and the fayḍa
entries.heading: Q. 5:45 (FIR 3:64–65)
entries.kind: commented. Not on any listed locus; found by search (raw l14.txt).
entries.niasse: After Jalālayn's gloss he states a rule for this community's law: «كل ما ذكر القرآن من حكم التوراة والإنجيل ولم يبين لنا نسخه فهو حكم لنا، هذا حكم لنا» ("whatever ruling of the Torah and the Gospel the Qurʾān mentions without showing us its abrogation is a ruling for us; this is a ruling for us"). He reads fa-man taṣaddaqa bihi both ways (the killer who gives himself up, the avenger who forgives) and draws the Mālik/Shāfiʿī dispute from it: «فقال الشافعي إن الحدود زواجر وقال مالك إن الحدود جوابر» ("al-Shāfiʿī said the ḥudūd are deterrents and Mālik said they are expiations"), and he holds the verse supports Mālik, with the story of the Ghāmidiyya (3:65).
entries.jalalayn: Read out: the retaliations, «وما لا يمكن القصاص فيه ففيه الحكومة في اجتهاد الإمام», and «وهذا الحكم وإن كتب عليهم فهو مقرر في شرعنا» (Hamza: "Although this stipulation was prescribed for them, it is established in our Law").
entries.sawi: The editor's n. 1 at the zawājir/jawābir dispute cites «حاشية الصاوي على تفسير الجلالين» 1:286 without quoting it (3:65).
entries.ruhAlBayan: RB vol 2, offset c. 1067200–1068400. Plain gloss: wa-l-jurūḥa qiṣāṣ where equality can be known, otherwise arsh or ḥukūma; fa-man taṣaddaqa = the one entitled who forgives, «فهو» أي التصدق «كفارة له» أي للمتصدق, with a second view (garbled in the OCR) that it expiates the offender. No statement on earlier law binding this community and no zawājir/jawābir debate. RB has a related line at Q. 2:4 from al-Taysīr: «الإيمان بما لم ينسخ من أحكامها».
entries.relation: Jalālayn: extends. Jalālayn's "established in our Law" for this one ruling becomes in Niasse a general principle (sharʿ man qablanā binds unless abrogated). RB: silent/not comparable on that principle at this verse. On fa-man taṣaddaqa Niasse keeps both readings where RB prefers the avenger, and he adds the legal-school dispute, which RB does not raise.

rulings.label: silent/not comparable on that principle at this verse

entries.section: 7.10 This community and the fayḍa
entries.heading: Q. 5:54 (FIR 3:70–74; locus 3:70–73)
entries.niasse: He reads the verse as a prophecy fulfilled: «هذه الآية نزلت قبل وقوع هذه القضية» (3:70). He narrates eleven apostate groups: three in the Prophet's lifetime (al-Aswad killed by Fayrūz, «رجل مبارك»; Musaylima and his letter; Ṭulayḥa), seven under Abū Bakr over zakāt, and one under ʿUmar (Jabala b. al-Ayham). On Abū Bakr: «فتقلد سيفه وحده» ("he girded on his sword alone"); «فكانوا كرهوا هذا الأمر في البداية وأحبود في النهاية» [read وأحبوه]; and he credits ʿUmar with «والله ما ولد مولود بعد الأنياء أفضل من أبي بكر الصديق» [read الأنبياء] (3:72). On the people God loves he gives three reports (the Yemenis, Salmān's people, Abū Mūsā's people) and adds his own gloss on Salmān: «إشارة لسود الجلود إذا آمنوا بالله» ("a pointer to the black-skinned when they believe in God"). His rule: «والعبرة بكل من اتصف بهذه الصفات» ("what counts is everyone who has these qualities"). He ends with a rebuke: «المسلمون عكسو» [عكسوا] «هذه القضية الآن هم أشداء على المسلمين رحماء بالنسبة إلى الكافرين» (3:73–74).
entries.jalalayn: Read out and once named: «إخبار بما علم اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى وقوعه», then «وقد ارتد جماعة قال جلال بعد موت النبي صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم» (the OCR places «قال جلال» inside the gloss), and «هم قوم هذا» pointing to Abū Mūsā. The editor identifies "Jalāl" as al-Suyūṭī (3:70 n. 1: «هو السيوطي في الجلالين ج289/1 من الحاشية»), so he reads Jalālayn in the Ṣāwī edition.
entries.sawi: No wording. The editor's references to the Ḥāshiya are bibliographic: 1:289 for the Jalālayn text (3:70 n. 1) and 1:291 at 3:74 n. 1 (the note's anchor is not visible in the OCR).
entries.ruhAlBayan: RB vol 2, offset c. 1085400–1089800. The same eleven groups in the same order: al-Aswad and Fayrūz «قتله رجل مبارك», Musaylima's letter and the reply «إن الأرض لله يورثها من يشاء من عباده والعاقبة للمتقين», Waḥshī «قتلت خير الناس في الجاهلية وشر الناس في الإسلام», Ṭulayḥa, and the zakāt-refusers: «أما الصلاة فنصلي وأما الزكاة فلا نغصب أموالنا»; «فتقلد أبو بكر سيفه وخرج وحده»; Ibn Masʿūd «كرهنا ذلك في الابتداء ثم حمدناه في الانتهاء»; «وقيل ما ولد بعد النبيين مولود أفضل من أبي بكر»; al-Ḥasan «لولا ما فعل أبو بكر لألحد الناس في الزكاة». The beloved people: Yemen («الإيمان يمان والحكمة يمانية»), the Anṣār, or Persia («لو كان الإيمان معلقاً بالثريا لناله أبناء فارس»). The Sufi layer: faḍl Allāh means some cross the path in twenty years and some in a moment «بتوفيق خاص وعناية سابقة», with Pharaoh's sorcerers and Ibrāhīm b. Adham as examples.
entries.relation: Jalālayn: extends (from Jalālayn's one-line "notification of what God knew" to the full narrative). RB: follows, closely and without naming it. Side by side: RB «أما الصلاة فنصلي وأما الزكاة فلا نغصب أموالنا» / Niasse «نقيم الصلاة كما قال الله، أما الزكاة فلا نُغصَب أموالنا»; RB «فتقلد أبو بكر سيفه وخرج وحده» / Niasse «فتقلد سيفه وحده»; RB (Ibn Masʿūd) «كرهنا ذلك في الابتداء ثم حمدناه في الانتهاء» / Niasse «كرهوا هذا الأمر في البداية وأحبود في النهاية» [read وأحبوه]; RB «ما ولد بعد النبيين مولود أفضل من أبي بكر» (anonymous «قيل») / Niasse puts it in ʿUmar's mouth. Niasse's own: the reading of Salmān as a sign for black-skinned believers, the rule that the qualities and not the lineage count, and the rebuke of present Muslims. He does not use RB's Sufi point that God's faḍl lets some cross the path in a moment, though it would fit the fayḍa.

rulings.label: follows, closely and without naming it

entries.section: 7.10 This community and the fayḍa
entries.heading: Q. 6:89–90 (FIR 3:150)
entries.niasse: «هذه الآية أدل دليل على أفضلية الرسول صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم على جميع الأنبياء والمرسلين» ("this verse is the clearest proof of the Messenger's superiority over all the prophets and messengers"). Each prophet had all praiseworthy traits but was known for one: Dāwūd and Sulaymān for gratitude, Ayyūb for patience, Mūsā for miracles, Zakariyyā, Yaḥyā and ʿĪsā for renunciation, Yūsuf «في بدايته صابر وفي نهايته شاكر». Since Muḥammad was told to follow them all, «هذا دليل على أنه أفضل منهم جميعا لأنه جمَّعَ فيه ما تَغرّق فيهم» ("this proves he is better than all of them, because he gathered in himself what was scattered among them" [read تفرّق]) (3:150).
entries.jalalayn: Read out: «بهذه الثلاثة» for bihā; the qawm entrusted with it = «هم المهاجرون والأنصار»; fa-bi-hudāhum = «طريقهم من التوحيد والصبر», «اقتد بهم جميعا».
entries.sawi: not quoted in FIR at this verse; Ḥāshiya not in hand.
entries.ruhAlBayan: RB vol 3, offset c. 165200–166600. The entrusted people are the Prophet's Companions. Hudāhum = their way in faith and the principles of religion, not the abrogable laws. Then: «واحتج العلماء بهذه الآية على أنه عليه السلام أفضل جميع الأنبياء عليهم السلام», because the traits were scattered: Dāwūd and Sulaymān thankful, Ayyūb patient, «ويوسف كان جامعاً بينهما», Mūsā «صاحب المعجزات القاهرة», Zakariyyā, Yaḥyā, ʿĪsā and Ilyās renouncers, Ismāʿīl truthful, «فجمع الله كل خصلة في حبيبه عليه السلام». The Taʾwīlāt najmiyya: each prophet's journey ended at his heaven; the Prophet is told to follow them all until he passes the Lote Tree to qāb qawsayn.
entries.relation: Jalālayn: follows (gloss read without change). RB: follows on the argument from scattered traits, nearly item for item. Niasse drops Ilyās and Ismāʿīl and adds his own line on Yūsuf (patient at the start, thankful at the end). RB's «احتج العلماء بهذه الآية» becomes Niasse's «أدل دليل». The ḥabīb frame («في حبيبه») is RB's. Niasse does not take up the Najmiyya miʿrāj reading.

rulings.label: follows on the argument from scattered traits, nearly item for item

entries.section: 7.10 This community and the fayḍa
entries.heading: Q. 6:89 (FIR 3:150)
entries.crossRef: See Q. 6:89–90 above; same locus. For fa-qad wakkalnā bihā qawman Niasse reads only Jalālayn («هم المهاجرون والأنصار»), where RB has "the Companions".

entries.section: 7.10 This community and the fayḍa
entries.heading: Q. 6:165 (FIR 3:189–90)
entries.niasse: He moves from Jalālayn's "succeeding one another" to a vicegerency from God: «فكل إنسان خليفة عن اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى على وجه الأرض في جزء من هذا العالم» ("every human is a vicegerent of God on the face of the earth over a part of this world"). Only Ādam and Dāwūd are named khalīfa in the Qurʾān, and «كلاهما فزع من الخلافة حتى تفرقت حروف اسمه» ("both took fright at the vicegerency, so that the letters of his name came apart"). He argues from lordship: «كلنا رب شيء ولو قليلا ولو صغيرا» ("each of us is lord of something, however little and small"). From there to this community: the Companions ruled the lands with no geometry, arithmetic or medicine, only verses they lived by; Muslims today have taken every science and left their book; air and sea are subjected to them more than to Sulaymān and Dāwūd, yet faith has not grown: «المادة قضت على الروح» ("matter has done away with the spirit"). He ends: «وإني أدعو إلى الرجوع إلى كتاب اللّٰه وإلى التمسك به» (3:189–90).
entries.jalalayn: Read out: «جمع خليفة يخلف بعضكم بعضا فيها»; darajāt glossed as «بعضهم يجد المال، وبعضهم يجد الجاه، وبعضهم لم يجد شيئا من ذلك» (Niasse's expansion of Jalālayn's "wealth and status and otherwise"); «ليظهر المطيع منكم والعاصي».
entries.sawi: not quoted in FIR at this verse; Ḥāshiya not in hand.
entries.ruhAlBayan: RB vol 3, offset c. 353300–355500. Khalāʾif = after the jinn, or after earlier nations, «أو خلفاء الله في أرضه تتصرفون فيها». Najmiyya: «هو جعل كل واحد من بني آدم آدم وقته وخليفة ربه في الأرض», the secret of vicegerency being that God formed him on the form of His attributes. Then the test of wealth and rank, a long ḥadīth on accounting for lawful wealth, the gift of «استعداد الخلافة», and Ibrāhīm b. Adham's story.
entries.relation: Jalālayn: corrects (from succession to vicegerency from God; Niasse keeps Jalālayn's gloss but argues past it). RB: selects among. The idea that every son of Ādam is a vicegerent is RB's third option and its Najmiyya reading («كل واحد من بني آدم آدم وقته وخليفة ربه»); Niasse states it without RB's "form of the attributes" theology and grounds it in ownership ("lord of something"). The separated letters of Ādam and Dāwūd and the lament over modern Muslims are Niasse's own; the lament repeats his introduction (FIR 1:55).

entries.section: 7.10 This community and the fayḍa
entries.heading: Q. 10:3 (FIR 4:158–61)
entries.kind: commented. Not on any listed locus; found by search (raw l23.txt).
entries.niasse: On "six days" he reads al-ān: «الآنُ الدائم هو حياة الحق» ("the enduring now is the life of the Real"), the now that stretches into a second, an hour, a day, a year, a thousand-year day, a fifty-thousand-year day, «هو هذا الآن فقط» ("it is only this now"), and «وإلى الآنِ يشير قوله "كُلَّ يَوْمٍ هُوَ مِي شَأْلِ"» (4:158). Creation ran Sunday to Friday; he lists what each weekday is for (Saturday "makr and deceit", Sunday building and planting, Monday travel, Tuesday blood, Wednesday answered prayer at the Trench, Thursday entering on kings, Friday marriage) (4:159). On the world's age: «وتلك الأيام سبعة والدنيا سبعة أيام» and «وقد مرت سبعة آلاف سنة وثلاثمائة واثنان وثمانون في هذا العام» (4:160; see Problems). After a-fa-lā tadhakkarūn: «وهذا تعليم للتأني» ("this is a lesson in deliberation"), with the ḥadīth on deliberation and six things in which haste is not from Satan (4:160).
entries.jalalayn: Read out: «من أيام الدنيا، أي في قدرها لأنه لم يكن ثم شمس ولا قمر، ولو شاء لخلقهن في لمحة»; yudabbiru l-amr «بين الخلائق»; «ردا لقولهم إن الأصنام تشفع»; «الخالق المدبر». Jalālayn's reason for the six days ("to teach His creatures circumspection") is moved by Niasse to after a-fa-lā tadhakkarūn as «وهذا تعليم للتأني».
entries.sawi: The editor cites «حاشية الصاوي على الجلالين ج78 /2» with Ibn Kathīr for creation beginning on Sunday and ending on Friday (4:158 n. 1). No wording.
entries.ruhAlBayan: RB vol 4, offset c. 17000–25000. Ḥaqqī gives the days: the first day created is Sunday; Saturday means rest, and the Jews' claim that God rested is denied; then the questions put to the Prophet about each day: «يوم مكر وخديعة» for Saturday «لأن قريشاً مكرت فيه في دار الندوة», Sunday «يوم غرس وعمارة», Monday travel, Tuesday «يوم دم» (Ḥawwāʾ's menses, Ādam's son killing his brother, Zakariyyā and Yaḥyā killed), Wednesday answered prayer against the Aḥzāb, Thursday entering on the sultan (Ibrāhīm and the king of Egypt, Hājar), Friday marriage (Ādam and Ḥawwāʾ). On yudabbiru l-amr the Najmiyya reads the Throne as the first receiver of the divine overflow: «لفيضان فيض رحمانية على العرش فإنه أول قابل لفيض الرحماني».
entries.relation: Jalālayn: follows, with a displacement (the "deliberation" reason moved and joined to a ḥadīth). RB: follows on the weekdays: the order, the reasons and the examples match. RB: departs on time. Niasse's "enduring now" as the life of the Real is not at this verse in RB. Ḥaqqī's nearest statement is at Q. 32:5 (RB vol 7, offset c. 273200), where the OCR shows him calling the day «كالآن» and linking it to kulla yawmin huwa fī shaʾn; the passage is badly damaged and I could not read it whole. Niasse ignores RB's fayḍ reading of the Throne here.

rulings.label: follows on the weekdays: the order, the reasons and the examples match

entries.section: 7.10 This community and the fayḍa
entries.heading: Q. 12:53 (FIR 5:39–40)
entries.niasse: Yūsuf spoke from humility: «ليست نفس يوسف من تلك الأنفس» ("Yūsuf's self was not one of those selves"); he knew «أن نفسه غير داخلة في هذا» and so did not say "my self is ammāra". Ammāra is intensive: «إن أمرت النفسُ بالسوء، تكون آمرة وإن أمرت به كثيرا تكون أمارة». The ascent is a series of overflows of mercy: «إذا جاءت الرحمة من الحضرة الإلهية وفاضت على النفس تنتقل من النفس الأمارة بالسوء إلى النفس اللوامة» ("when mercy comes from the divine Presence and overflows onto the self, it passes from the self commanding evil to the blaming self"), then mulhama, then, «إذا استمرت عليها فيوضات الرحمة», muṭmaʾinna, rāḍiya, marḍiyya, kāmila. «هي سبعة مقامات» (5:40). «سلوك غير الأنبياء من النفس الأمارة بالسوء إلى أن تصل إلى الكمال، وسلوك الأنبياء من النفس المطمئنة إلى الكمال». He links Q. 6:112: the self is the devil among humans, «فهي أعدى عدو للإنسان», and gives the hierarchy «الروح هو السلطان والعقل هو الوزير والقلب هو المفتي», followed by the fable of the three oxen and the lion (5:40).
entries.jalalayn: Read out: «من الزلل»; «جنس النفس صفتها أنها تأمر بالسوء كثيرا»; «إلا من رحم ربي فعصمه» (5:39).
entries.sawi: not quoted in FIR at this verse; Ḥāshiya not in hand.
entries.ruhAlBayan: RB vol 4, offset c. 724300–728600. Exoteric: humility; the lām is generic, «أي جميع النفوس التي من جملتها نفسي في حد ذاتها»; «أمرت النفس بشيء فهي آمرة وإذا أكثرت الأمر فهي أمارة». Najmiyya: when the dawn of guidance breaks the self becomes lawwāma, then mulhama, then muṭmaʾinna when «شمس العناية» reaches mid-heaven. Ḥaqqī's own: «سلوك الأنبياء عليهم السلام وإن كان من النفس المطمئنة إلى الراضية والمرضية والصافية», but every self, prophets' included, is ammāra by nature; hence «ولذا لم يقل يوسف عليه السلام إن نفسي لأمارة بالسوء» and Ibn al-Shaykh «فأئبت الأمارية لنفس يوسف» [read فأثبت]. Najm al-Dīn on Q. 6:112: «فشيطان الإنس نفسه الأمارة بالسوء وهي أعدى الأعداء». Nafāʾis al-majālis: «سلطان الروح ووزير العقل ومفتي القلب», then the fable of three oxen and a lion.
entries.relation: Jalālayn: follows. RB: follows on most of the material and corrects on one point. Shared: the āmira/ammāra distinction; the ladder; the prophets' path starting from muṭmaʾinna; 6:112 and "worst enemy"; the sultan-vizier-mufti triad; the oxen fable. Side by side: RB «سلوك الأنبياء عليهم السلام وإن كان من النفس المطمئنة» / Niasse «وسلوك الأنبياء من النفس المطمئنة إلى الكمال»; RB «وهي أعدى الأعداء» / Niasse «فهي أعدى عدو للإنسان». The correction: Ḥaqqī insists that Yūsuf's self too is ammāra by nature and is only kept from acting; Niasse says Yūsuf's self is outside the class and that Yūsuf knew it. Niasse also names the seventh stage kāmila where Ḥaqqī has ṣāfiya, and he describes each step as an overflow (fayḍ) of mercy, where the Najmiyya uses the image of the sun of ʿināya.

rulings.label: follows on most of the material and corrects on one point

entries.section: 7.10 This community and the fayḍa
entries.heading: Q. 16:8 (FIR 5:128–29; also cited at 3:126)
entries.niasse: Wa-yakhluqu mā lā taʿlamūn covers ships «في البحر والبر والهواء» and then the saints: «لهذا الرسول صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم استكفى عن الخلافة. لم يستخلف أحدا على أمته عند وفاته لأنه علم أن في أمته من يأخذ العلم من اللّٰه بلا واسطة» ("this is why the Messenger did without naming a successor: he appointed no one over his community at his death, because he knew that in his community are those who take knowledge from God without intermediary"), and so said «اللّٰه خليفتي على كل مسلم». The saint «يتلقى العلم من اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى بلا واسطة كما تلقاه الملك الذي أنزل على الرسول وكما تلقاه الرسول، ولكنه غير مستقل» ("receives knowledge from God without intermediary, as the angel sent down to the Messenger received it and as the Messenger received it, but he is not independent"); «فليس للولي أن يأتي بحكم جديد» ("the saint may not bring a new ruling"); «ولكنه يأخذ من المعدن الذي أخذ منه النبي ومن المعدن الذي أخذ منه الملك». Finally: «بعد فناء وجود العبد وبقاء الحق تبارك وتعالى من علوم ومشاهدات وأسرار لا يعلمها إلا اللّه» ("after the passing away of the servant's existence and the subsistence of the Real, of sciences, witnessings and secrets that only God knows") (5:129). At 3:126 he cites the verse for al-Shāfiʿī's answer that land and sea vessels are included, and adds that he has "a second answer"; the next page goes on to Q. 15:21.
entries.jalalayn: Read out: «من الأشياء العجيبة» [الغريبة] (5:128–29).
entries.sawi: not quoted in FIR at this verse; Ḥāshiya not in hand. (The editor's notes here are on the Prophet's mounts and on the ḥadīth «الله خليفتي على كل مسلم» from Muslim.)
entries.ruhAlBayan: RB vol 5, offset c. 28500–31000. Exoteric: insects, sea creatures, creatures beyond Qāf, the thousand nations. Najmiyya: «ويخلق فيكم بعد رجوعكم بالجذبة إلى مستقركم ما لا تعلمون قبل الرجوع إليه وهو قبول فيض نور الله تعالى بلا واسطة». Ibn ʿArabī: «سكت النبي عليه السلام عن الاستخلاف إذ في أمته من يأخذ الأمر عن ربه», who «يأخذ من المعدن الذي يأخذ منه الملك والموحى إلى الرسول والمعدن الذي يأخذ منه الرسول», but «والخليفة الولي ليس كذلك ناقص عن رتبة النبوة». Ḥaqqī closes: «فانظر إلى استعداد كامل هذه الأمة كيف أخذوا الفيض من الله بلا واسطة».
entries.relation: Jalālayn: extends. RB: follows, very closely and without naming it. The silence about succession, the saint taking from the same "mine" as the angel and the Prophet, the saint's dependence, and the fayḍ "without intermediary" after the return by jadhba are all in RB (Ibn ʿArabī and the Najmiyya). Side by side: RB «سكت النبي عليه السلام عن الاستخلاف إذ في أمته من يأخذ الأمر عن ربه» / Niasse «لم يستخلف أحدا على أمته عند وفاته لأنه علم أن في أمته من يأخذ العلم من اللّٰه بلا واسطة»; RB «يأخذ من المعدن الذي يأخذ منه الملك» / Niasse «ومن المعدن الذي أخذ منه الملك». Niasse adds the ḥadīth «الله خليفتي على كل مسلم» as a proof-text, which RB does not use, and he states the limit as a legal rule (no new ruling). He also replaces RB's jadhba with "the passing away of the servant's existence and the subsistence of the Real". This is the clearest place in the section where RB's "this community takes fayḍ without intermediary" enters FIR.

rulings.label: follows, very closely and without naming it

entries.section: 7.10 This community and the fayḍa
entries.heading: Q. 27:92 (FIR 7:111–12; locus 7:112)
entries.niasse: «أمرني أن أستمر على دراسة القرآن» and «فتلاوة القرآن أفضل العبادات مطلقا» (7:111). The disciple's arc: «والمريد في بداية انتباهه تحدثه نفسه أنه مشتغل في شيء أعظم من تلاوة القرآن» ("the disciple at the start of his awakening tells himself he is busy with something greater than reciting the Qurʾān"), «ولكن عند الكمال يرجع إلى القرآن فيجد القرآن مادة كل مقام، ومادة كل خير، ومادة كل عبادة، ومادة كل علم دنيوي أو أخروي» ("but at perfection he returns to the Qurʾān and finds it the substance of every station, every good, every act of worship, every worldly or otherworldly knowledge") (7:111). Reading from the muṣḥaf is better: the eye, the hand, the finger tracing word by word, the ear, the tongue and the heart each worship (7:112). «فأكبر نعمة عند الملائكة سماع القرآن». Then the chain of hearing: hear the Qurʾān «من الرباني أولا ثم من المرتبة التي فوق الرباني حتى تسمع من رسول اللٰه صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم حتى تسمع من المتكلم بالقرآن وهو رب العزة» (7:112).
entries.jalalayn: Partly read: «تتبع القرآن بالتلاوة للدعوة إلى اللّٰه» echoes Jalālayn's "as a call to faith"; the rest is Niasse.
entries.sawi: Quoted by the editor (7:111 n. 1): «وقال الصاوي في حاشيته على الجلالين: وفي هذه الآية إشعار أن تلاوة القرآن أعظم العبادات قدرا عند الله» (Ḥāshiya 3:207). This matches Niasse's «فتلاوة القرآن أفضل العبادات مطلقا». The editor also identifies "al-Rabbānī" as a Mauritanian ḥāfiẓ who «هاجر إلى الشيخ ابراهيم رضي اللّٰه عنه إبان ظهور الفيضة» (7:112 n. 2).
entries.ruhAlBayan: RB vol 6, offset c. 991000–993600. «أي وأمرت بأن أواظب على تلاوته لتكشف لي حقائقه», the reason the sages made it their last wird: «المنكشف أولاً للعارفين حقائق الآفاق ثم حقائق الأنفس ثم حقائق القرآن». Then: «ولا تهجره كما يفعل ذلك طلبة العلم وبعض المتصوفة زاعمين بأنهم قد اشتغلوا بما هو أهم من ذلك وهو كذب فإن القرآن مادة كل علم في الدنيا». Reading from the muṣḥaf: «ويضع يده على الآية يتبعها» so that tongue, eye and hand each take their share; «وسماع القرآن أشرف أرزاق الملائكة» (from the Futūḥāt).
entries.relation: Jalālayn: extends. al-Ṣāwī (via the editor): follows. RB: follows, with close verbal overlap. RB «زاعمين بأنهم قد اشتغلوا بما هو أهم من ذلك» / Niasse «تحدثه نفسه أنه مشتغل في شيء أعظم من تلاوة القرآن»; RB «فإن القرآن مادة كل علم في الدنيا» / Niasse «مادة كل علم دنيوي أو أخروي»; RB «وسماع القرآن أشرف أرزاق الملائكة» / Niasse «فأكبر نعمة عند الملائكة سماع القرآن»; RB the hand on the verse following it / Niasse the finger tracing word by word. Niasse turns Ḥaqqī's polemic against Sufis who neglect the Qurʾān into a stage of the path (beginning, then return at perfection). The chain of hearing, from one's own Qurʾān teacher up to the divine Speaker, is his own. The editor's note links it to the fayḍa through al-Rabbānī.

entries.section: 7.10 This community and the fayḍa
entries.heading: Q. 32:5 (FIR 7:209)
entries.kind: commented. Not on any listed locus; found by search (raw l40.txt).
entries.niasse: Before the verse he raises the community's lifespan: «وقد اختلفوا في الصدر الأول هل أمة محمد يبلغون الألف أم لا يبلغون الألف حتى ألف السيوطي وهو في القرن التاسع كتابا سماه «الكشف في مجاوزة الأمة الألف»» [quoted without the inner title: see below] and «وقد جاوزت الألف الآن وزادت تقريبا أربعمائة سنة لابد من التزود لعل الأمر قرب» ("it has now passed the thousand and gone beyond by about four hundred years; one must lay in provision; perhaps the matter is near"). He reads yudabbiru l-amr as «مدة الدنيا وهي سبعة أيام» and distinguishes the thousand-year day from the fifty-thousand-year Day, which for the believer is «أخف عليه من صلاة مكتوبة يصليها في الدنيا». Some are spared the station: «إن لله عبادا ليسوا بأنبياء ولا شهداء يغبطهم الأنبياء والشهداء» (7:209).
entries.jalalayn: Read out: "for the duration of this world" (Niasse adds «وهي سبعة أيام»); the Maʿārij fifty thousand years as the severity for the unbeliever and the lightness for the believer, «كما ... في الحديث» (Hamza); Niasse keeps all of this.
entries.sawi: not quoted in FIR at this verse; Ḥāshiya not in hand. (The editor cites al-Ṣāwī 3:260–61 earlier in the sūra, on the munjiyāt, not at this verse.)
entries.ruhAlBayan: RB vol 7, offset c. 271200–273800. The four angels who manage affairs; the thousand years as the descent and ascent of the angel; an alternative that God manages the world for its duration and then on the Day «ينفرد الله بالأمر», the Day being heavy for the unbeliever «ويسهل على المؤمنين حتى يكون كقدر صلاة مكتوبة». Ḥaqqī's own note on "day" as an indivisible "now" (damaged). Najmiyya: the self's ascent by jadhba, «جذبة من جذبات الحق توازي عمل الثقلين».
entries.relation: Jalālayn: follows. RB: silent/not comparable on the community's age, which is the point Niasse makes; on the fifty-thousand-year Day Niasse and RB both follow Jalālayn. The al-Suyūṭī treatise and the reckoning to his own day are Niasse's. With Q. 5:19 and 10:3 this gives a consistent chronology: the world is seven "days" of a thousand years, and this community has passed its thousand.

rulings.label: silent/not comparable on the community's age, which is the point Niasse makes

entries.section: 7.10 This community and the fayḍa
entries.heading: Q. 40:1 (FIR 8:159–61; locus 8:161)
entries.niasse: On ḥā mīm he gives the ḥadīths on the Ḥawāmīm, Ibn ʿAbbās's view that alif-lām-rāʾ, ḥā-mīm and nūn together make al-Raḥmān, and «وقيل "جم" رمز من رموز المحبين يتكلمون فيما بينهم بألفاظ هي سر عندهم» ("it is said that ḥā mīm is one of the lovers' codes; they speak among themselves in words that are a secret to them"); «"جمّ" جزء من الرحمن وجزء من محمد». Then the story: Mūsā asked whether God had honoured anyone as He honoured him; God answered with a community honoured by Ramadan: «أنا كلمتك من وراء سبعين ألف حجاب، وهم إذا صاموا أرفع عنهم الحجب فأكون أقرب إليهم من كل شيء» ("I spoke to you from behind seventy thousand veils; when they fast I lift the veils from them and am nearer to them than anything"), «وإذا حان الفطور ألقاهم مواجهة» ("and when the time to break the fast comes I meet them face to face"). Niasse adds: «فهناك لقاء عند الفطور يختص به الصائمون» ("so there is a meeting at the breaking of the fast proper to those who fast"). Mūsā asked for the month for his people; «هو لأمة محمد صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم» (8:160–61).
entries.jalalayn: «اللّٰه أعلم بمراده به» (Hamza: "God knows best what He means by these"), read twice (8:160).
entries.sawi: not quoted in FIR at this verse; Ḥāshiya not in hand.
entries.ruhAlBayan: RB vol 8, offset c. 397500–400900. Ḥā mīm as a divine name and key to His treasures; Ibn ʿAbbās on the letters of al-Raḥmān; Najmiyya: «الحاء والميم هما حرفان من وسط اسم الله وهو رحمن وحرفان من وسط اسم نبيه وحبيبه محمد», an oath by a secret between God and His beloved; «حم لا ينصرون». The Kashf al-asrār passage (Persian) on this community receiving unasked, ending «أعطيتكم قبل أن تسألوني». Then the Mūsā story: «إن لي عباداً أخرجهم في آخر الزمان وأكرمهم بشهر رمضان», «فإني كلمتك بيني وبينك سبعون ألف حجاب», the veils lifted «وقت إفطارهم», «فإني لا أجازيهم دون لقائي», and «هذه لآمة محمد». The editor cites this RB passage (8:161 n. 1: «انظره في روح البيان ج150 /8»).
entries.relation: Jalālayn: extends (keeps the tafwīḍ formula and adds what others said). RB: follows. The secret of ḥā mīm shared by al-Raḥmān and Muḥammad is the Najmiyya's; Niasse's «رمز من رموز المحبين» restates RB's «القسم بسر بينه وبين حبيبه». The Mūsā–Ramadan story is RB's, and the editor says so. Niasse sharpens it: RB's "I will not reward them short of meeting Me" becomes «ألقاهم مواجهة», a face-to-face meeting at iftar that belongs to those who fast.

entries.section: 7.10 This community and the fayḍa
entries.heading: Q. 40:8 (FIR 8:165–66)
entries.kind: commented. Not on a listed locus; found by search (raw l44.txt).
entries.niasse: He tells how the believer in Paradise asks for his father, wife and children, who did not reach his rank, and God has them brought: «يقول الرب: آتوه بأبيه إني لا أحب غضب وليي اليوم» ("the Lord says: bring him his father, for I do not like My friend to be angry today") (8:165). Then the extension: «وكما تلحق الذرية بالنسب تلحق الذرية بالمعنى. التلامذة يلحقون بمراتب أشياخهم. كلنا في مقام الشيخ التجاني رضي اللّٰه عنه» ("as offspring are joined by lineage, offspring are joined by meaning: disciples are joined to the ranks of their shaykhs. We are all in the station of Shaykh al-Tijānī") (8:166). He adds the ḥadīth on having many brothers in God.
entries.jalalayn: Read out: «جنات إقامة»; al-ʿazīz al-ḥakīm «في صنعه».
entries.sawi: not quoted in FIR at this verse; Ḥāshiya not in hand. (The editor sources the Paradise story to al-Ṭabarī from Saʿīd b. Jubayr, 8:165 n. 1.)
entries.ruhAlBayan: RB vol 8, offset c. 422800–424300. Wa-man ṣalaḥa = those whose righteousness suffices for entry, «وإن كان دون صلاح أصولهم», to complete their joy; «وفيه إشارة إلى أن بركة الرجل التائب تصل إلى آبائه وأزواجه وذرياته»; Saʿīd b. Jubayr's report («إني كنت أعمل لي ولهم»); a ḥadīth on children leading parents into Paradise. Najmiyya: «أنت العزيز تعز التائبين وتحبهم».
entries.relation: Jalālayn: extends. RB: extends. Niasse shares RB's report from Saʿīd b. Jubayr and its ishāra that a man's blessing reaches his kin. He then moves from kin by blood to kin by meaning: disciples joined to their shaykhs, and "all of us" in al-Tijānī's station. This step is not in RB. It is the section's most direct statement that the Tijānī community shares its founder's rank.

entries.section: 7.10 This community and the fayḍa
entries.heading: Q. 42:13 (FIR 8:211–16; locus 8:214)
entries.niasse: On aqīmū l-dīn wa-lā tatafarraqū: unity is in creed, not in branches: «عدم التفرق ليس في الفروع، التفرق في الفروع ليس بمذموم» (8:213), citing «اختلاف أمتي رحمة». On Allāhu yajtabī ilayhi man yashāʾ wa-yahdī ilayhi man yunīb he sets out two roads (the OCR line is damaged: see Problems). The people of election: «أما أهل الاجتباء والجذب فأحبهم اللّه بمشيئته فأخذ بقلوبهم وأوصلهم إلى حضرته من غير تكلف منهم بل قطع لهم المسافة بالمعونة لا بالمؤنة. هذه الأمة أمة محمد» ("as for the people of election and attraction, God loved them by His will, took their hearts and brought them to His Presence without effort on their part; He covered the distance for them by assistance, not by toil. This community is the community of Muḥammad") (8:214). Then the same Ibrāhīm / Mūsā / night journey / Q. 41:53 sequence, and a typology: «فهما قسمان: سالك ومجذوب، فالسالك ما لم يجد جذبا فهو محجوب ولو عبد عبادة الثقلين» ("there are two kinds, the wayfarer and the attracted; the wayfarer who has found no attraction is veiled, even if he worshipped with the worship of jinn and humans"); the attracted man without wayfaring benefits himself only, with Ibn ʿArabī's verse «لا تقتدي بالذي زالت شريعته / عنه ولو جاء بالأنبا عن الله»; «والسالك الجذوب كامل، مجذوب سالك كامل، سالك غير مجذوب ظاهري، مجذوب غير سالك مجذوب أبتر» (8:215). All prophets are majdhūb, returned to their sharīʿa; Ibrāhīm's «هذا ربي» means "my witnessed one" (with the grammatical argument from hādhā rather than hādhihi), and Mūsā's sobering at "what is that in your right hand?" (8:215–16).
entries.jalalayn: Read out: «هو أول أنبياء الشريعة» for Nūḥ; «هذا هو المشروع الموصى به والموحى إلى محمد صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم وهو التوحيد»; yajtabī ilayhi «إلى التوحيد»; man yunīb «يقبل على طاعته» (8:211–14).
entries.sawi: not quoted in FIR at this verse; Ḥāshiya not in hand. (The editor's n. 1 at 8:213 quotes al-Thaʿālibī on tafarruq in creed, not al-Ṣāwī.)
entries.ruhAlBayan: RB vol 8, offset c. 799400–803800. Prophets agree in the principles and differ in branches (Q. 5:48); «فإن يد الله ونصرته مع الجماعة»; Sahl on the inner sharīʿas of the prophets; «فالولي الكامل يجب عليه متابعة العمل بالشريعة المطهرة». On yajtabī: «واجتباء الله تعالى العبد تخصصه إياه بفيض إلهي يتحصل منه أنواع من النعم. بلا سعي من العبد», for prophets and those near them. Najmiyya: «يشير بقوله الله يجتبي إليه الآية إلى مقامي المجذوب والسالك», the majdhūb drawn «بجذبة توازي عمل الثقلين», the sālik moved by effort and ināba.
entries.relation: Jalālayn: extends (Jalālayn's "to tawḥīd" stays; the Sufi reading is added). RB: extends. The majdhūb/sālik pair at this verse and the election "without effort by the servant" are RB's (Najmiyya and Ḥaqqī's gloss: «بلا سعي من العبد» / Niasse «من غير تكلف منهم»). Niasse brings in the maʿūna/maʾūna sequence from RB's Q. 4:28 ishāra. He moves election from "prophets and those near them" (RB) to "this community, the community of Muḥammad". He adds the four-fold typology and Ibn ʿArabī's verse, and he reverses the Najmiyya's praise of the jadhba "equal to the deeds of jinn and humans": a sālik without jadhba stays veiled even with "the worship of jinn and humans". On tafarruq he follows Jalālayn and RB.

entries.section: 7.10 This community and the fayḍa
entries.heading: Q. 56:1–33 (no FIR text)
entries.kind: not found in FIR. The commentary on Q. 56:1–33 stood on pp. 168–69, which are missing from the raw export (Lesson 49 dossier §11). The OCR passes from the sūra heading on p. 167 to «مَرْمُوعَةٍ» (56:34) on p. 170. I found no citation of these verses elsewhere in FIR.
entries.jalalayn: (Hamza) the foremost are the prophets; the multitude from the former; the few from the later = from Muḥammad's community.
entries.sawi: not quoted in FIR at this verse; Ḥāshiya not in hand.
entries.relation: not comparable (Niasse's text lost).

entries.section: 7.10 This community and the fayḍa
entries.heading: Q. 56:10–14 (no FIR text)
entries.kind: not found in FIR (lost pp. 168–69, as above). Searches for «السابقون السابقون», «ثلة من الأولين» and «وقليل من الآخرين» find only the ḥadīth «نحن الآخرون السابقون» (FIR 1, Lesson 4; 3, Lesson 15; 10:11 at Q. 62:9) and the bare Jalālayn text of 56:39–40 at 9:170.
entries.jalalayn: (Hamza) al-sābiqūn = the prophets; "a multitude from the former"; "a few from the later ones, from among the community of Muḥammad".
entries.sawi: not quoted in FIR at this verse; Ḥāshiya not in hand.
entries.ruhAlBayan: RB vol 9, offset c. 824600–833200. Ḥaqqī's shaykh divides servants into people of forgetfulness, of remembrance and of iḥsān; the third «أهل الحضور مطلقا» are the sābiqūn. Ḥaqqī argues that this community's foremost are more numerous: the Prophet likened its scholars to the prophets of the Israelites, and «أن أولياء في كل عصر من أعصار هذه الأمة عدد الأنبياء وهم مائة ألف وأربعة وعشرون ألفا», including «الغوث والأقطاب والكمل». Najmiyya: the few of the later are «المحمديين» with «التجليات الذاتية».
entries.relation: not comparable at this verse. For the dissertation: Niasse uses RB's comparison of this community's scholars with Israelite prophets at Q. 5:44 («علماء أمتي كأنبياء بني إسرائيل», FIR 3:64), and RB's Wāqiʿa note is the obvious source to check if the lost pages turn up.

entries.section: 7.10 This community and the fayḍa
entries.heading: Q. 56:88–89 (FIR 9:174)
entries.niasse: He glosses al-muqarrabīn as «من عباد اللّٰه الصالحين» and adds a prayer: «جعلنا اللّٰه من أهل ذلك» ("may God make us among its people") (9:174). Nothing more.
entries.jalalayn: Read out: «فله استراحة» for rawḥ, «رزق حسن» for rayḥān. Niasse omits Jalālayn's grammatical note on whether the apodosis belongs to ammā or in.
entries.sawi: not quoted in FIR at this verse; Ḥāshiya not in hand.
entries.ruhAlBayan: RB vol 9, offset c. 883300–885200. Rawḥ as rest and mercy; Abū l-ʿĀliya: none of the muqarrabūn leaves the world before smelling the rayḥān of Paradise; «فله روح الوصال وريحان الجمال وجنة الجلال»; for the muqarrabūn this already holds in this world, «وروحهم المشاهدة وريحانهم سرور الخدمة».
entries.relation: Jalālayn: follows (with a cut). RB: silent/not comparable; Niasse uses none of RB's Sufi reading. His gloss "God's righteous servants" is broader than Jalālayn's and RB's sense of "those brought near".

entries.section: 7.10 This community and the fayḍa
entries.heading: Q. 62:2 (FIR 10:4–6; locus 10:6)
entries.niasse: Ummī is praise in the Prophet's case: «وإن كان أميا علِم علم الأولين والآخرين» (10:5). Teaching: «أما الصحابة فقد تلقوا هذا منه بلا واسطة وعلّم التابعين وتابعي التابعين وهلم جرا ولكن بوسائط، بوسائط العلماء» ("the Companions received this from him without intermediary, and he taught the Successors, their Successors and so on, but through intermediaries, the intermediaries of the scholars"); «فالنبي صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم هو المعلم في كل زمان حتى ينقضي الدهر في زمانه بلا واسطة وفي زماننا بوسائط العلماء» (10:5). Each teacher goes back to the Prophet, «فهو المعلم الكبير»; then «الشريعة بالنسبة للعوام والطريقة بالنسبة للخواص والحقيقة بالنسبة لأخص الخواص» (10:6). On wa-in kānū min qablu la-fī ḍalālin mubīn: with an Arab prophet and an Arabic Qurʾān «صار العرب أفضل الأجناس» (10:6).
entries.jalalayn: Read out: «العرب»; «محمدا صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم»; «يطهرهم من الشرك»; al-ḥikma «ما في القرآن من الأحكام والشرائع» (10:4).
entries.sawi: not quoted in FIR at this verse; Ḥāshiya not in hand. (Editor's notes: Lisān al-ʿArab, al-Baghawī, the ḥadīth «العلماء ورثة الأنبياء».)
entries.ruhAlBayan: RB vol 9, offset c. 1334200–1336800. Yuzakkīhim carries «إشارة إلى قاعدة التسليك», the perfect human as locus of the divine attributes. On teaching: «لكن معلم الصحابة عموماً وخصوصاً هو النبي عليه السلام بلا واسطة ومعلم التابعين قرناً بعد قرن هو عليه السلام أيضاً لكن بواسطة ورثة أمته وكمل أهل دينه وملته». Al-Būṣīrī's line on knowledge in an unlettered man as a miracle.
entries.relation: Jalālayn: follows and extends. RB: follows, with close verbal overlap. RB «معلم الصحابة عموماً وخصوصاً هو النبي عليه السلام بلا واسطة ومعلم التابعين قرناً بعد قرن هو عليه السلام أيضاً لكن بواسطة ورثة أمته» / Niasse «أما الصحابة فقد تلقوا هذا منه بلا واسطة وعلّم التابعين وتابعي التابعين وهلم جرا ولكن بوسائط، بوسائط العلماء». Niasse adds the shariʿa/ṭarīqa/ḥaqīqa triad for three classes of people, and his "Arabs the best of races" follows RB's later remark on 62:3 that knowing the Arabs' merit is a condition of religion.

entries.section: 7.10 This community and the fayḍa
entries.heading: Q. 62:3 (FIR 10:6–7)
entries.niasse: Wa-ākharīna minhum lammā yalḥaqū bihim = «عطف على الأميين الموجودين، سيأتي رجال آخرون من تلك الطبقة ولم يدركوا ماهم» (10:6). He tells the Prophet's dream of black sheep followed by white, Abū Bakr's reading (Arabs, then non-Arabs) and the Prophet's «بهذا أوله الملك» (10:6–7). Then: «إن هنالك رجالا في أصلاب الرجال وفي أرحام الأمهات يدخلون الجنة بلا حساب ولا عقاب», the Prophet's hand on Salmān, «وما في المسجد رجل أسود إلا سلمان», and «وهذا بشارة للمسلمين الذين دخلوا الإسلام من البلاد العجمية» ("this is good news for the Muslims who entered Islam from non-Arab lands") (10:7).
entries.jalalayn: Read out in part: «عطف على الأميين الموجودين» (Hamza: "a supplement to al-ummiyyīna, those who are alive"). Niasse drops Jalālayn's restriction to the Successors and its rider that every generation is better than the next.
entries.sawi: not quoted in FIR at this verse; Ḥāshiya not in hand.
entries.ruhAlBayan: RB vol 9, offset c. 1336800–1339000. Al-Kāshifī: all who enter Islam after the Prophet, «من عربي وعجمي»; the ḥadīth «إن في أصلاب رجال من أمتي رجالاً ونساء يدخلون الجنة بغير حساب»; the dream of black and ʿufr sheep and «أولها الملك»; then «وقيل لما يلحقوا بهم في الفضل والمسابقة» and «ومن شرائط الدين معرفة فضل العرب على العجم». On 62:4 Ḥaqqī adds God's favour «بإرسال ورثة محمد في كل عصر إليهم».
entries.relation: Jalālayn: corrects (Niasse leaves out the Successors and the decline of generations and reads the verse forward to future non-Arab believers). RB: follows for the material (the same ḥadīth and dream, in the same order) and selects among for the sense: Niasse takes Kāshifī's open reading (all later converts) over the reading "not equal in merit". His "only Salmān was black in the mosque" and "good news for the ʿAjam" are his own and carry the point he made at Q. 5:54.

entries.section: 7.10 This community and the fayḍa
entries.heading: Q. 62:9 (FIR 10:11–14; locus 10:14)
entries.niasse: «يوم الجمعة هو يوم المسلمين. هذا اليوم الذي اختلف فيه الأمم قبلكم فاهتديتم إليه. فنحن الاخرون السابقون» (10:11). The wisdom of Friday: God made the world from Sunday to Friday and then brought the human, so the human owes a feast of thanks (10:12). Islam's three feasts each mark the completion of a worship: «والمسلمون عيدهم عند تمام عبادتهم» (10:13). After these, the mawlid: «ما كان القرون الثلاثة يقومون بهذا العيد، أحدث بعد القرون الثلاثة، وهو أفضل ما أحدث لهذه الأمة، وجربوا بركته» ("the first three generations did not keep this feast; it was introduced after them, and it is the best thing introduced for this community, and they have tried its blessing") (10:14).
entries.jalalayn: Read out: «اتركوا البيع والشراء» [Jalālayn: suspend contracts]; «أنه خير فافعلوه» (10:11).
entries.sawi: not quoted in FIR at this verse; Ḥāshiya not in hand. (The editor cites RB for the custom of a meal after Friday prayer, 10:13 n. 1: «ذكره البروسوي في روح البيان ج522/9».)
entries.ruhAlBayan: RB vol 9, offset c. 1355000–1366000. Ḥaqqī's ishāra reads the dispersal after prayer as dispersal in the inner earth; from al-Ashbāh he lists Friday's properties, including «وهو خير أيام الأسبوع ويوم عيد». I did not find a mawlid passage at this verse.
entries.relation: Jalālayn: follows. RB: extends. Friday as a feast is in RB's list from al-Ashbāh. The account of feasts as completions of worship and the mawlid as the best innovation of this community are Niasse's.

entries.section: 7.10 This community and the fayḍa
entries.heading: Q. 89:23 (FIR 10:180–82)
entries.kind: commented. Not on a listed locus; found by search (raw l55.txt).
entries.niasse: He narrates the gathering, the tenfold rings of jinn and angels around humanity, God's manifestation «بصفته المنتقم», Hell made small "like a puppy" and brought on seventy thousand reins, the prophets each saying «نفسي نفسي», and the Prophet: «جهنم تأتي للمحشر قبل أن آخذ أمتي؟ ما يمكن هذا» ("Hell comes to the gathering before I have taken my community? That cannot be"). He prostrates and is opened with praise: «قلت إن الفتح لا ينتهي حيث أن رسول اللّٰه صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم لم يزل يفتح له في ذلك المقام» ("I have said that the opening never ends, since the Messenger is still being opened to in that station"). He strikes Hell so it flees seventy thousand years, and intercedes first for the prophets, then scholars, then martyrs (10:181–82).
entries.jalalayn: Read out: «تقاد بسبعين ألف زمام كل زمام بأيدي سبعين ألف ملك» and «لها زفير وتغيظ» (10:180).
entries.sawi: not quoted in FIR at this verse; Ḥāshiya not in hand. (The editor sources the reins ḥadīth to Muslim, 10:180 n. 1.)
entries.ruhAlBayan: RB vol 10, offset c. 1114200–1116000. Wa-jīʾa as "made visible", or literal. Ibn Masʿūd and Muqātil: seventy thousand reins, seventy thousand angels each; Hell bolts and would burn the gathering; every prophet and saint kneels saying «نفسي نفسي» «حتى يعترض لها رسول الله كَل ويقول أمتي أمتي», and the Fire says «لقد حرم الله لحمك علي». Ḥaqqī's own: Hell's coming may be its imaginal form, like the Aqṣā brought before the Prophet's eyes.
entries.relation: Jalālayn: follows and extends. RB: extends. Both make the Prophet stand alone against Hell while others say "myself". Niasse's version is a full intercession narrative (Hell shrunk, the Prophet strikes it, intercession for prophets first) that is not in RB here. His remark that the Prophet's opening "never ends" is his own.

entries.section: 7.10 This community and the fayḍa
entries.heading: Q. 110:1–3 (FIR 10:221)
entries.niasse: Mūsā had one enemy and lived in fear; Muḥammad «كلف بالتبرئة من جميع من يعبد غير اللّٰه فصار العالم كلا عدوا له» ("was charged with disowning all who worship other than God, so the whole world became his enemy"); asked what he would have, God answered "the help of God and the opening". Had Mecca been opened and its people scattered, nothing would have come of it; but they entered «أفواجا أفواجا». Then: «وعده بالنصر وكلفه التسبيح لأن التسبيح في مقابلة النصر، لا ناصر إلا اللّٰه» ("He promised him help and charged him with glorification, because glorification answers help: there is no helper but God"); praise answers the opening; and since crowds entering the religion «هذا فيه داع لتكبر النفس أو رؤية النفس فأمر بالاستغفار» ("this calls the self to pride or to seeing itself, so he was commanded to seek forgiveness") (10:221).
entries.jalalayn: Read out in part: "for His Prophet"; "in throngs" (Niasse doubles «أفواجا أفواجا»). Niasse omits Jalālayn's dates (conquest in Ramadan 8, death in Rabīʿ I 10) and its report that the sūra announced the Prophet's death.
entries.sawi: not quoted in FIR at this verse; Ḥāshiya not in hand.
entries.ruhAlBayan: RB vol 10, offset c. 1362900–1368600. Naṣr attributed to God because the believers' motives are created; the fatḥ of Mecca as «مفتاح الفتوح». From the Iṣṭilāḥāt: three openings (the near opening of the heart, the clear opening of sainthood, the absolute opening of the Essence «بفناء الرسوم» [الخلقية كلها]). Tasbīḥ as wonder, prayer or tanzīh; al-Suhaylī on why praise always follows glorification. Istighfār: «هضماً لنفسك واستقصاراً لعملك»; he glorified God before looking at the people «لأنه رأى الله قبل رؤية الناس».
entries.relation: Jalālayn: selects among. RB: selects among. Niasse's pairing (tasbīḥ with naṣr, ḥamd with fatḥ) and his reason for istighfār (the crowds tempt the self to see itself) are close in sense to RB's «هضماً لنفسك», but I find no verbal overlap. The Mūsā/Muḥammad contrast (one enemy against the whole world) is not in RB at this sūra. Niasse ignores RB's three openings.

sectionNotes.section: 4.3 What God wills and what He approves
sectionNotes.heading: Findings for sections in this block
sectionNotes.text: - Niasse's account of the "two stations" at 8:17 comes from al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya as Ḥaqqī quotes it: killing denied entirely to the Companions, throwing affirmed and denied for the Prophet, who "threw by God". Niasse names the pair «المقامين» and adds a grammatical proof (FIR 4:39; RB 3, p. 955). - On human action he takes RB's map at 4:88 whole: Jabriyya, Qadariyya, «الجبر المتوسط» (his «جبر صغير»), the ʿārifūn's vision that "is not jabr", and the pairing of 32:11 with 39:42. His own addition is that the ʿārifūn unite the two errant creeds, figured as milk between dung and blood (16:66). The same middle path, in RB's own list of means, returns at 16:90. - The will/approval distinction (6:148, 16:35, 43:20, 39:7) is Jalālayn's. Niasse grounds it in an argument of his own: creatures will only what benefits them, so their will and approval coincide; God has no benefit, so He wills what He does not approve. He names this «خطاب المشيئة وخطاب الحكمة» (6:148) and «أمر إرادي» ... «وأمر شرعي» (20:123). RB analyses the same verses formally (two premises; will as tarjīḥ) but has neither the analogy nor the two commands. - RB supplies many of Niasse's Sufi readings near-verbatim: the covenant's three ranks and «بالجود لا بالوجود» (7:172), the human's need of God's essence where other creatures need only His acts (35:15), signs and karāmāt as tarbiya for their age (6:111), the lovers' code of the letters (19:1), the Yūnus proof of no place (2:115), the "wa" and nuzūl-as-iqbāl (3:17), the four classes of saʿīd and shaqī (from RB 6:37, used at 7:56 and 59:16–17), the "Zayd died" analysis (46:3), and ʿālam al-amr as free of evil (113:2). He never names RB in his own voice; the editor's footnotes name it at 4:7, 6:41, 6:35, 7:52, 7:69 and 3:192. - Where he takes RB's material he often moves its ground. At 7:172 the third rank answers "by imitation", not "under compulsion"; the four classes rest on pre-eternal decree with works as signs (3:210; 10:189), never on Ḥaqqī's istiʿdād

sectionNotes.heading: Findings for sections in this block
sectionNotes.text: - Niasse's Sufi readings in this group very often come from Rūḥ al-bayān, mostly from the "Taʾwīlāt najmiyya" and "baʿḍ al-kibār" layers, and he does not name the source; the editor sometimes does. Word-level borrowing is clear at Q. 6:160 (the ten prior ḥasanāt, with ḥidāya in place of rizq), 9:36 (a third of life for God), 9:111 (Iblīs's objection, «في مذهب من المذاهب»), 13:39 (three tiers of maḥw, ending in «الوجود/الجود»), 15:49–50 ("He did not say 'I am the one who punishes'"; fear and hope as wings), 21:22 (the complete and deficient gods), 35:15 (only man needs the Essence), 112:1 (huwa, Allāh, aḥad as three stations, from Ibn al-Shaykh via RB). - Niasse takes RB's material and changes where it sits on the path. At Q. 40:60 (with 2:186, 14:35) Ibrāhīm's "His knowledge of my state is enough" is Ḥaqqī's station of the perfected; Niasse makes it Ibrāhīm's beginning and makes the perfected gnostic return to supplication out of courtesy. At Q. 12:33 Yūsuf's choice is made a mark of his state "before his perfection". At 15:49–50 and 55:27 he adds a stage above RB's jamāl/jalāl pair: kamāl muṭlaq. - Niasse corrects Jalālayn openly and by name more than once: Q. 2:21 (laʿalla as the servant's hope, against «المفسر»), 6:128 («ليس بمرضي جدا»), 23:86 (ʿarsh is not kursī), 57:4 (evil deeds do not ascend; maʿiyya is by essence, not knowledge). Where he does not correct, he reads the gloss out and builds on it (most verses in 4.4, 4.10, 4.11). - al-Ṣāwī reaches FIR only through the editor in this group. The one substantive case is Q. 11:107, where Niasse quotes «المفسر» (the editor: al-Ṣāwī 2:229) on the exit «من الجحيم إلى الزمهرير» and replaces it with his own view («والحق...»). sectionNotes.section: 4.17 What the close readings add up to
sectionNotes.heading: Findings for sections in this block
sectionNotes.text: - Niasse's deepest borrowings from RB come from its Sufi layers, mostly TN and Ḥaqqī's anonymous «بعض الكبار», and he never names them. Clear cases: the three-rank tawḥīd from the "human tree" (Q. 28:30, reused at Q. 16:2); the need of the Essence peculiar to the human (Q. 35:15); the three groups and three resurrections (Q. 4:87); "the word is true, its meaning false", with the same "Zayd died" example (Q. 46:3); "rūʾya with the eye of the head" and "in this world with the eye of the eye" (Q. 10:26); the Companions/Prophet contrast in "you did not throw" (Q. 8:17); the a fortiori line «لقطع طمع قومه» (Q. 7:143, Q. 4:153). - He also takes over RB's exoteric philology where it serves kalām: idrāk is not ruʾya (Q. 6:103, which corrects the gloss «لا تراه»); naẓar is turning the pupil (Q. 7:143); al-Irshād's seven seas that pour into the encircling sea (Q. 31:27); Ibn al-Shaykh's "had God known" as more eloquent than "had there been" (Q. 8:23), which becomes the thesis «شيئا لم يعلمه الله لا وجود له». - He leaves RB where Ḥaqqī's verdict limits what a saint may claim or hear: he keeps the seventy as hearers of divine speech that RB's Taysīr denies (Q. 2:75); he keeps the Iblīs story RB rejects (Q. 7:143); he gives ʿinda rabbika a non-spatial reading against RB (Q. 11:83); he reads min at Q. 53:18 as partitive, which Ḥaqqī rejects, to rank Muḥammad over Abraham. - On maʿiyya he departs from RB's exoteric layer every time (Q. 7:7, 26:15, 50:16, 57:4, 58:7) and from its rule of concealment: Ḥaqqī says the essential maʿiyya must be hidden and "preservation or command" taught instead (Q. 57:4); Niasse states the Essence view openly and refutes the "effects of His power" view. His proofs from Q. 7:7 (two clauses) and Q. 56:85 (tubṣirūn, not taʿlamūn) are not in RB. Yet at Q. 56:85 in sequence he lets Jalālayn's «لا تعلمون» stand, a tension inside FIR. - He corrects Jalālayn by name or by "al-mufassir" where the gloss blocks his theology: maʿiyya "by knowledge" (Q. 50:16, 57:

sectionNotes.section: 5.1 The Spirit at Q. 17:85 and the Divine Breath
sectionNotes.heading: Findings for sections in this block
sectionNotes.text: - RB is Niasse's main unnamed source for the anthropology, and he takes over RB's wording. Close verbal overlap at Q. 2:30 (seal; jāʿil as ʿālam al-amr), 2:260 (the seven vices paired as spouses), 3:33–37 (the parents' food and intention form the child), 7:172 (three rows; «بالجود لا بالوجود»; al-Junayd), 12:53 (ladder of the self (nafs); sultan–vizier–mufti; the three bulls), 13:39 (three-tier maḥw/ithbāt), 17:85 (synonyms of the two worlds; first-creation names; «آدم أبو البشر ومحمد أبو الأرواح»), 35:15 (only the human needs the Essence), 41:53 (microcosm list, near verbatim), 90:4 (life as toil; pleasure as relief from pain). The editor's footnotes often point to the RB page while Niasse speaks without naming it. - Niasse takes from RB's Najmiyya layer far more than from its exoteric layer, and sometimes rejects the exoteric layer without saying so: the real pre-existential address at 7:172 against RB's tamthīl; «من روحي» as the Muḥammadan rūḥ against RB's ishtiʿāl reading at 32:9 and 38:72. - The Muḥammadan rūḥ is the point where Niasse goes beyond RB. RB states it once (at 17:85, vol 5); Niasse applies it at every nafkh verse (4:171, 7:11–12, 7:189, 32:9, 66:12), makes Jibrīl a recipient rather than the breather, names it «الحقيقة المحمدية», and at 3:11 and 66:12 concludes that Muḥammad is ʿĪsā's real father. At 95:4 he adds a bodily counterpart: the human frame spells "Muḥammad". - He corrects RB on prophetic ʿiṣma (12:53: Yūsuf's self is not ammāra even by nature) and inverts RB's labels for the two spirits in sleep (39:42), keeping Jalālayn's tamyīz/life distinction. - He corrects Jalālayn openly, naming al-mufassir: 76:1 (120 years, not 40); 17:85 (the verse defines the rūḥ instead of withholding it, after the Najmiyya); 2:115 («قبلته» labelled the interpreters' taʾwīl); 41:30 (angels may descend on saints in life). Elsewhere (2:260, 7:189, 15:44, 23:12–14, 38:71) he follows Jalālayn silently, including details RB rejects (the prostration as a bow). - His "

sectionNotes.text: - Niasse's Sufi readings of the faculties come largely from RB, unnamed and often in RB's own words: the twelve springs as five outer senses, five inner senses, nafs and qalb (2:60); the nafs/qalb/rūḥ/sirr place values of reward (6:160); one garment per faculty (7:26); the āmira/ammāra derivation, the ladder of nafs stations, the prophets' path beginning at the muṭmaʾinna, the sultan-vizier-mufti image and the three-bulls fable (12:53, with 6:112 via Najm al-Dīn Dāya). - His doctrine of khilāfa is built from RB's Taʾwīlāt and RB's quotation of al-Rāghib: jāʿil not khāliq (2:30); the spirit succeeds God because both lack place and direction, which he moves from RB's 2:30 to 2:115; the four reasons for khilāfa and the four classes of religious men (24:55, nearly verbatim); the praise reading of ẓalūm jahūl and the ʿajz formula (33:72). - His own additions are Tijānī or Muḥammadan, and they come at the end of RB's material: the Seal of the Saints read out of 24:55; al-quṭbāniyya al-ʿuẓmā as the trust (33:72) and as the one rank women cannot reach (33:35); al-Tijānī's two ignorances joined to RB's jahūliyya (6:54, 33:72); the five presences of the Prophet as khalīfa and «وأخفَى من السر هو الله» (20:7); the spirit breathed into Adam, Maryam and every nuṭfa as Muḥammad's spirit (4:171, 66:12); «محمد رسول الله» as God's reply at the covenant (48:29). - On need (35:15) and the covenant (7:172) RB supplies the central claims: only the human needs the Essence, the rest need only the acts; God took the nonexistent from the nonexistent, «بالجود ... لا بالوجود». Niasse replaces RB's lover-and-sultan image with Q. 5:54 and makes the third covenant row unbelievers who answered by taqlīd. - The proof that earth is better than fire (38:71–76, promised at 7:12) is RB's quotation of Ākām al-marjān point by point, reordered. - Where Niasse leaves RB he does so deliberately: he denies that Yūsuf's nafs was ammāra (12:53), against Ḥaqqī's explicit thesis built on 12:22 and 12:33; he make

sectionNotes.section: 5.6.1 God Honours the Children of Adam, Q. 17:70
sectionNotes.heading: Findings for sections in this block
sectionNotes.text: - Niasse reads the Jalālayn gloss nearly word for word at almost every verse and seldom marks a disagreement. He settles or corrects it at a few points: walāya "is correct" for al-Khiḍr (Q. 18:65); he rejects al-Maḥallī's "the Qurʾān is the truth" in the first person and reads "God is the Real" (Q. 41:53); he drops Jalālayn's clause that angels rank above non-prophet humans (Q. 17:70) and answers it at Q. 81:22; he drops "the Unseen" from the gloss at Q. 4:113. Where Jalālayn and RB differ, he usually keeps Jalālayn: sun as mother at Q. 12:5, "women of her time" at Q. 3:42. - His largest debt is to the Sufi layer of RB, mostly Najm al-Dīn's Taʾwīlāt. He takes over its full schemes, often with matching wording: the four elements, seven vices and seven gates (Q. 2:260, 15:44, 15:47); the stations of the self (nafs) (Q. 12:53, 75:2); the three rows and creation from nothing at the covenant (Q. 7:172); tafakkur and tadhakkur (Q. 13:19); the grades of the unseen (Q. 27:65); the three kinds of creature (Q. 3:95); blame and praise in "ẓalūm jahūl" (Q. 33:72); the khalīfa as image of the seven attributes (from Q. 6:165, used at Q. 2:115). - He also takes whole arguments from the compiled exoteric layers of RB without naming them. Examples: bukhl and ḥasad, envy as wanting to depose God, "the envier never leads" and the three kingships (Q. 4:53–54, reused at 1:124–27 and Q. 113:5); weakness and the ḥadīth qudsī (Q. 4:28); need of the essence (Q. 35:15); the microcosm list (Q. 41:53); kibr and istikbār (Q. 16:22–23); ʿAṭāʾ's minimums (Q. 33:35); daughters first (Q. 42:49–50). - He moves RB stories from one verse to another. The ten deceived go from Q. 2:4 to 2:22, the seven gatekeeper angels from 2:21 to 2:22, and the seven taught by God from 27:15 to 2:31 and 18:65. Others stay where RB has them: the three wishes (Q. 2:228), the indebted poor man and Yūnus (Q. 2:115), the bulls and the lion (Q. 12:53), the moon fatwa (Q. 95:4). sectionNotes.heading: Findings for sections in this block
sectionNotes.text: - Niasse's two-tier theory of walāya (walāya ṣughrā by any trait the Qurʾān or sharīʿa praises; walāya kubrā by eye-witness maʿrifa) appears at 3:17, 10:62–64 and 42:28. Its seed is RB's grammatical point at 3:17 that the wāw makes each praised quality independently praiseworthy; the two-tier division itself, and the claim that the greater walī shares the lesser's works but not the reverse (42:28), are not in RB, Jalālayn or what the editor cites from al-Ṣāwī. - Niasse takes RB's wording silently and often: the poverty and obscurity of saints as God's custom (10:2), fear and grief defined by future and past (10:62), the gnostic as the permanently needy whose prayer is answered (27:62), love of saints as not shirk and God's question "did you befriend a friend for Me?" (3:92, from RB at 3:95), Moses' deputy Hārūn against the Prophet's "God is my successor" (7:142), "fighting God is fighting His saints" (5:33, from RB's ishāra), every prophet, walī and ṣiddīq given an enemy (25:31), Āṣaf's throne annihilated and re-created (27:40), the "four enemies" with weapon and prison (16:99, RB elsewhere), and David's marriage without waiting for Jibrīl's leave (4:163). - Where he takes RB's material he usually changes its use: the Israelite who kissed the Prophet's name is forgiven in RB but becomes a walī in Niasse (33:40); "God is my successor" is explained by saints who receive knowledge without intermediary (7:142, 9:92, 16:8), which RB does not say; RB's "inspiration remains after prophecy" (10:64) becomes "the door of prophecy closed, the door of walāya opened" (4:179; 8:223). - On protection he corrects RB: RB defines ḥifẓ as abstaining from sin while sin remains possible; Niasse makes the walī protected from the evil effect of sin (hardness of heart, turning away), not from sin itself, and defines ʿiṣma as an essential incapacity "like a man's inability to fly" (38:24; 2:220). sectionNotes.heading: Findings for sections in this block
sectionNotes.text: - The section's controlling idea, that this community travels "by assistance, not by toil" (bi-l-maʿūna lā bi-l-maʾūna), comes from Ḥaqqī's ishāra on Q. 4:28 (RB vol 2, offset c. 521100): the four favours, the four proof-texts (37:99, 7:143, 17:1, 41:53) and al-wuṣūl wa-l-wiṣāl. Niasse uses it at 4:28 in RB's order and moves it to 2:253 (FIR 2:7) and 42:13 (FIR 8:214). He drops RB's rider that the saint arrives only by following the Prophet. - Niasse takes RB's "without intermediary" (bi-lā wāsiṭa) language for this community at two verses. At 16:8 (FIR 5:129) he takes Ibn ʿArabī's reading of the Prophet's silence on succession and the saint drawing from the angel's "mine" and adds «الله خليفتي على كل مسلم». At 62:2 (FIR 10:5) he takes "the Companions without intermediary, later generations through the heirs" almost word for word. - Niasse goes past RB where the community's rank reaches the Tijāniyya. Examples: "the perfect one of his age" at 2:4, "disciples are joined to the ranks of their shaykhs; we are all in al-Tijānī's station" at 40:8 (FIR 8:166), and election moved from "prophets and those near them" to "this community" at 42:13. None of these steps is in RB. - Long narrative and argument blocks follow RB closely without naming it: the eleven apostasies at 5:54 (verbal matches on Abū Bakr's sword, the zakāt refusers, "disliked at first, praised at the end"); the scattered traits of the prophets at 6:89–90; the weekdays at 10:3; the ladder of the self, the sultan/vizier/mufti triad and the oxen fable at 12:53; Qurʾān recitation at 27:92; the Ramadan story at 40:1. Only at 40:1 does the editor name RB. - Niasse corrects RB at 12:53. Ḥaqqī insists Yūsuf's self is ammāra by nature; Niasse says it is outside the class. At 4:28 he also replaces RB's and Jalālayn's Magians with "a faction of Quraysh". - Niasse follows Jalālayn silently at most commented verses and reads the gloss before his own comment (2:106, 2:253, 5:19, 5:54, 6:89–90, 10:3, 12:53, 56:88–89, 62:2
